Return JSON 401 from APIs and redirect HTML pages appropriately.\n131: - [ ] Create LiteChat-styled signup/login templates with validation/error states; implement logout as a CSRF-protected POST action.\n132: - [ ] Keep login, signup, logout, `next` redirects, templates, CSS, JS, and forms compatible with `/proxy/5001/`.\n133: - [ ] Add and test `DJANGO_APP_BASE_PATH` handling for templates and authentication redirects so `/accounts/...`, `/profile/`, `/billing/`, assets, and API calls remain inside `/proxy/5001/`; retain root behavior when the setting is `/`.\n134: \n135: ### C. Models and Ownership Migration\n136: \n137: - [ ] Add `UserProfile` one-to-one with the active auth user model; include `display_name` and a per-user `system_prompt` text field with an empty default.\n138: - [ ] Add one-to-one `BillingAccount` with account name `Personal`, `USD` currency, active/inactive status, `DecimalField` available balance defaulting to `2.00`, and timestamps; add a non-negative balance constraint and no payment fields.\n139: - [ ] Add a nullable owner FK to `Conversation` first; choose restrictive user-deletion behavior until an explicit account-deletion policy exists.\n140: - [ ] Provision the bootstrap superuser's profile and `Personal` ACTIVE USD `$2.00` billing account using an explicit idempotent setup step.\n141: - [ ] Make conversation listing, detail, continuation, and retry owner-scoped; set owner from `request.user` at creation and reject any submitted owner IDs.\n142: - [ ] Add the explicit legacy-owner management command; require the bootstrap username when unowned rows exist, assign every existing conversation to that account, and preserve all messages and conversation metadata.\n143: - [ ] Verify legacy row counts/ownership on a database copy, then add a later migration making owner non-null only after the human mapping is complete.\n144: - [ ] Do not mark migration tasks complete if deployed database backup, owner assignment, or row-integrity verification is unavailable.\n145: \n146: ### D. Profile, Prompt, and Billing Behavior\n147: \n148: - [ ] Implement `/profile/` reading only `request.user`; display name, username, user ID, and `date_joined`; allow changes only to display name and that user's system prompt.\n149: - [ ] Implement `/billing/` by resolving only `request.user.billing_account`; display `[Personal] <display name>`, status, and USD available credit.\n150: - [ ] Keep billing read-only/display-only: no purchases, cards, payment gateways, subscriptions, invoices, automatic credits, or chat gating based on status/balance.\n151: - [ ] Load the profile's current system prompt for that user's future proxy requests, including future turns in existing chats, without persisting it as a user/assistant transcript message or rewriting history.\n152: - [ ] Map the prompt correctly in OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google-compatible request formats and keep it out of all other users' requests and browser-visible configuration.\n153: \n154: ### E. Documentation\n162: \n163: - [ ] Document account creation/login/logout, session configuration, signup access policy, and protected routes.\n164: - [ ] Document per-user conversation ownership and 404 behavior for cross-user IDs.\n165: - [ ] Document profile fields and that user ID/member-since are read-only.\n166: - [ ] Document the simulated billing model, chosen unit/seed, absence of real payments, and whether balance affects chat.\n167: - [ ] Document legacy data mapping to the bootstrap superuser and the backup/restore procedure.\n168: - [ ] Document per-user system prompt storage, provider-specific handling, and access restrictions if included.\n169: - [ ] Reconcile known limitations and CodeRange subpath setup with tested implementation; never describe unverified flows as working.\n170: \n171: ## Testing\n172: \n173: - Signup: successful creation, duplicate username, password mismatch/weak password, password hashing, optional display name, atomic profile/account creation, bootstrap superuser setup, and idempotent related-record provisioning.\n174: - Login/logout: valid/invalid credentials, database session, POST logout with CSRF, session flush, private page denied after logout, safe `next` redirect handling.\n175: - Protection: anonymous access to workspace/profile/billing and all chat APIs; intended public signup/login/health/static routes; JSON 401 contract.\n176: - Ownership: create sets current user; history scoped to current user; detail/continue/retry foreign UUID denied with same 404 as unknown IDs; forged owner fields ignored/rejected.\n177: - Profile: own page shows display name/username/user ID/member-since; display-name and prompt update persist; a client cannot update another user's profile, username ownership, member date, or staff flags.\n178: - Global system prompt: persists across requests/reloads, applies only to owning user's generation, does not alter stored transcript, is not exposed to another user, and maps correctly to OpenAI/Anthropic/Google request schemas.\n179: - Billing: account created once per user, `Personal`/`ACTIVE`/`USD`/`$2.00` display, no negative balance, no cross-user reads/updates, and no purchase or payment side effects.\n180: - Legacy migration: empty DB path;       "text": "from django.db import IntegrityError, transaction\nfrom django.test import TestCase\n\nfrom chat.models import Conversation, Message\n\n\nclass WorkspaceFoundationTests(TestCase):\n    def test_home_page_renders_workspace(self):\n        response = self.client.get(\"/\")\n\n        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)\n        self.assertContains(response, \"LiteChat\")\n        self.assertContains(response, \"New conversation\")\n\n    def test_health_check_returns_ok(self):\n        response = self.client.get(\"/healthz/\")\n\n        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)\n        self.assertEqual(response.json(), {\"status\": \"ok\"})\n\n    def test_conversation_delete_cascades_to_messages(self):\n        conversation = Conversation.objects.create(\n            title=\"A thread\",\n            provider=\"openai\",\n            model_id=\"gpt-5.6-luna\",\n        )\n        first = Message.objects.create(\n            conversation=conversation,\n            role=Message.Role.USER,\n            content=\"Prompt\",\n        )\n        second = Message.objects.create(\n            conversation=conversation,\n            role=Message.Role.ASSISTANT,\n            content=\"Reply\",\n            provider=\"openai\",\n            model_id=\"gpt-5.6-luna\",\n        )\n\n        self.assertEqual(list(conversation.messages.all()), [first, second])\n        conversation.delete()\n        self.assertEqual(Message.objects.count(), 0)\n\n    def test_message_role_is_constrained_in_database(self):\n        conversation = Conversation.objects.create(\n            title=\"A thread\",\n            provider=\"openai\",\n            model_id=\"gpt-5.6-luna\",\n        )\n\n        with self.assertRaises(IntegrityError), transaction.atomic():\n            Message.objects.create(\n                conversation=conversation,\n                role=\"system\",\n                content=\"Not an allowed role\",\n            )",

Every conversation in the SQLite database is visible to anyone who can reach this app. It must be deployed behind private access control. The proxy key values are never stored in the repository or returned to the browser.\n9: \n10: The app uses Python's standard-library `urllib` for outbound proxy requests; it does not require a provider SDK or a separate HTTP-client dependency.\n11: \n12: ## Local Setup\n13: \n14: Create and activate a virtual environment, install dependencies, and configure Django settings in the process environment:\n15: \n16: ```bash\n17: python3 -m venv .venv\n18: source .venv/bin/activate\n19: pip install -r requirements.txt\n20: \n21: export DJANGO_DEBUG=true\n22: export DJANGO_SECRET_KEY='local-development-only-change-me'\n23: export DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS='localhost,127.0.0.1'\n24: export DJANGO_SQLITE_PATH=''\n25: \n26: python manage.py migrate\n27: python manage.py check\n28: python manage.py test\n29: python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000\n30: ```\n31: \n32: Use `BUILD_OPENAI_KEY`, `BUILD_ANTHROPIC_KEY`, and/or `BUILD_GOOGLE_KEY` as needed. Set actual values only in a private shell/runtime secret configuration. `.env.example` contains placeholders; this project does not load `.env` files automatically. An unset key leaves that model disabled in the selector.\n33: \n34: SQLite defaults to `db.sqlite3` in the project directory. `DJANGO_SQLITE_PATH` can point to a writable persistent location; an empty value uses the default. Local database files are ignored by Git.\n35: \n36: ## Runtime Settings\n37: \n38: - `DJANGO_DEBUG`: defaults to `false`. Set `true` only for local development. If `false`, startup requires `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY`.\n39: - `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY`: Django signing/session secret. Keep it private and out of Git.\n40: - `DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`: comma-separated host names; configure for the actual deployment host.\n41: - `DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`: comma-separated full origins when the deployment's HTTPS/reverse-proxy setup requires them.\n42: - `DJANGO_SQLITE_PATH`: optional SQLite file path. The default is `<project-root>/db.sqlite3`.\n43: - `BUILD_OPENAI_KEY`: server-side key for the proxy's OpenAI-compatible interface.\n44: - `BUILD_ANTHROPIC_KEY`: server-side key for the proxy's Anthropic-compatible interface.\n45: - `BUILD_GOOGLE_KEY`: server-side key for the proxy's Gemini-compatible interface.\n46: \n47: The proxy key names and request formats are documented at <https://proxy.litechat.ai/docs>. Do not put their values in templates, JavaScript, browser storage, source files, or logs.\n48: \n49: ## Migrations and Tests\n50: \n51: After model changes, create/review migrations and apply them:\n52: \n53: ```bash\n54: python manage.py makemigrations\n55: python manage.py migrate\n56: python manage.py test\n57: ```\n58: \n59: The default test suite mocks the proxy boundary and makes no live or paid provider requests.\n60: \n61: ## CodeRange\n62: \n63: The CodeRange app target is `0.0.0.0:5001`, mounted at `/proxy/5001/`.
